topics.title: National Affairs: BRICS, Arunachal Talks, WDFC and Major Policy Updates
facts: The 18th BRICS Summit began in New Delhi on 12 September 2026; India held the 2026 chairship under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”.
The summit highlighted expanded BRICS membership, partner countries, political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and cultural and people-to-people cooperation.
India and China held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in the Arunachal Pradesh sector, linked to the Wacha and Damai border meeting points and continuing LAC dialogue.
The final sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor were dedicated to the nation, completing the JNPT/Navi Mumbai–Dadri connectivity; related projects were valued at about ₹20,700 crore.
The 7th Global Fintech Fest 2026 was held in Mumbai under the theme “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum – Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance”.

The 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah was launched for 9 September–8 October 2026 under the theme “Hamari Anganwadi Hamari Jimmedari”, with focus on nutrition, protein, fresh meals, community ownership and early childhood development.
PM-SETU approved strategic investments of ₹735.70 crore for ITI clusters at Bhiwadi, Medchal and Meerut; cumulative sanctioned investment reached about ₹2,171 crore across nine clusters.
DILRMP 3.0 received an outlay of ₹565.50 crore for 2026–31, including a GIS-based integrated Land Stack and 14-digit Bhu-Aadhaar/ULPIN for land parcels.

Proposed Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules amendments require clearer sponsored-listing disclosure, search-result fairness and current-versus-previous price transparency; the new rules are to apply from 1 January 2027.
Digital Bharat Nidhi and Jharkhand signed an agreement under the Amended BharatNet Programme involving about ₹1,684 crore, 4,395 Gram Panchayats and nearly 26,777 villages.
NSO released district-level estimates for the unincorporated non-agricultural sector using ASUSE 2025 data for January–December 2025, covering establishments, workers and GVA.
topics.detail: The week combined major diplomatic and infrastructure developments with nutrition, land-record modernisation, digital connectivity, e-commerce regulation and district-level economic data.
topics.exam: BRICS chairship and theme, LAC dialogue, dedicated freight corridors, POSHAN, PM-SETU, ULPIN, BharatNet and ASUSE are relevant for UPSC, UPPSC, SSC, Banking and CDS/NDA.

topics.title: International Affairs: BRICS, Correct the Map and Health Cooperation
facts: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi with resilience, innovation, sustainability and Global South cooperation as key themes.

The UN General Assembly adopted the “Correct the Map” resolution by 164–1; the initiative was led by Initiative Africa and Togo and promoted projections that show relative continental size more accurately.

The 79th session of the WHO South-East Asia Regional Committee was held in Dili, Timor-Leste, from 7–10 September and produced the Dili Declaration on Human Resources for Health: Equity in Specialized Care.

The WHO session covered medical devices, diagnostics, health-facility resilience, patient and blood safety, TB elimination, and viral hepatitis, HIV and STI responses; India received recognition for maternal and neonatal tetanus elimination and NCD screening.
The UN General Assembly declared 27 November the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage; Sierra Leone led the resolution and about 70 countries co-sponsored it.

MAHE, IIT Madras and IISc Bengaluru were selected as host institutions for the 2026–27 US–India Fellowship covering AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, biotechnology, energy, defence and space technology.
topics.detail: International developments focused on multilateral reform, fair map representation, specialised healthcare, child-marriage prevention and India–US academic and technology cooperation.
topics.exam: UN resolutions, WHO regional committees, international days, BRICS and India–US technology partnerships are useful for UPSC GS-2, UPPSC, SSC and Banking.
topics.remember: Correct the Map vote: 164–1; WHO RC79: Dili; Child Marriage Day: 27 November; Fellowship hosts: MAHE, IIT Madras and IISc.

topics.title: Economy, Banking and Business: Forex, Ratings, MSME Finance and Partnerships
facts: India’s foreign-exchange reserves reached a record high of about US$785.7 billion in the week ending 4 September, rising by nearly US$45 billion in one week; RBI inflows between 5 June and 31 August were about US$136.3 billion.
Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India’s sovereign rating by one notch to A, citing growth, consumption, investment, financial-sector strength and a lower NPA ratio.
The Ministry of Finance secured about US$1 billion in IFC-linked long-term credit support for MSMEs; US$500 million was routed to SIDBI and the balance is to come through a lender syndicate.
ADB signed its first Transaction Advisory Services mandate in India with Madhya Pradesh for renewable-energy PPPs, solar and battery storage, with potential private investment of about US$1 billion.

RBI added Coastal Local Area Bank, Vijayawada, to the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934; it was described as India’s first Local Area Bank and gained better access to RBI liquidity and money-market facilities.
NPCI International and Singapore-based FOMO Pay partnered to enable UPI QR acceptance for Singapore merchants, allowing Indian tourists to pay through UPI while merchants receive SGD settlement.

ONGC announced an Alternative Investment Fund of about ₹2,000 crore for deep-tech energy startups, covering AI subsurface intelligence, drilling, hydrogen, mobility, CBG, refinery technology and digital asset management.

JSW Group and Volkswagen Group signed a proposed 51:49 India passenger-vehicle JV focused on EVs, hybrids, ICE vehicles, localisation, manufacturing and R&D, with possible capacity of four lakh vehicles annually.
Qualcomm and AWS partnered on customised AI chips, AI inference and high-speed optical connectivity for AWS data centres; the stated optical capability was about 1.6 Tbps.
Bandhan Bank and Mastercard launched four credit-card variants: Sparks, Ignite, Flare and Lumina.
topics.detail: The week brought record forex reserves, a sovereign-rating upgrade, large MSME and renewable-energy financing arrangements, new payment connectivity and technology/manufacturing partnerships.
topics.exam: Remember the forex figure, JCR rating, IFC–MSME funding, Coastal Local Area Bank, UPI–Singapore, ONGC AIF and proposed JSW–Volkswagen ratio for economy and banking questions.
topics.remember: Forex: US$785.7 billion; JCR India rating: A; IFC-linked MSME support: US$1 billion; ONGC AIF: ₹2,000 crore.

topics.title: Science and Technology: CE20, Ocean Research, AI, Chips and Space Technology
facts: ISRO conducted a successful hot test of the CE20 cryogenic engine at Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu, at 220 kN thrust; the engine uses LOX and LH2 and is linked to the upgraded LVM3 C32 stage and Gaganyaan-related LTPM demonstration.
ORV Sagar Manthan, an advanced Ocean Research Vessel, was launched at an estimated cost of ₹840 crore; GRSE built it for NCPOR under the Deep Ocean Mission and commissioning is expected in 2028.

The India Photonics Association was launched as an ecosystem-led industry body focused on industry–academia collaboration, research, policy support and photonics innovation; the market was estimated at US$78.4 billion in 2025 and about US$155 billion by 2034.
IIT Madras and UNESCO MGIEP partnered on AI-based immersive learning using extended reality, game design and social-emotional learning for personalised and gamified education.
AI-driven agriculture tools are being developed for crop monitoring, pest and disease prediction, yield prediction, stress detection and farm decision support.

Karnataka led the ChipIN Centre initiative with 81 organisations, 73 chip tape-outs and about 88 lakh EDA tool-use hours; Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh were also major contributors.
Qualcomm and AWS collaborated on custom AI silicon and optical networking for hyperscale AI data centres.
Samtel Avionics and Japan’s BULL Co. signed an MoU on space-debris mitigation, including post-mission disposal, active debris removal and sustainable orbital operations.
German startup Isar Aerospace launched the Spectrum rocket on the Onward and Upward mission from Andøya Spaceport, Norway, carrying multiple CubeSats.
Apollyon Dynamics’ Ahuti Mk II multirotor UAV reached a certified top speed of about 498 km/h and was described as India’s fastest multirotor UAV.
The 2026 Ig Nobel Chemistry Prize recognised research on high-energy protein crystals in the milk-like secretion of the Pacific beetle cockroach; the ceremony was held in Zurich.
topics.detail: The technology news cycle covered cryogenic propulsion, ocean research, photonics, immersive education, agricultural AI, semiconductor design, orbital sustainability, private spaceflight, UAVs and unusual chemistry research.
topics.exam: CE20, Sagar Manthan, ChipIN, Spectrum, Ahuti Mk II and space-debris mitigation are high-value science and technology revision points.
topics.remember: CE20: 220 kN; Sagar Manthan: ₹840 crore; ChipIN leader: Karnataka; Spectrum: Isar Aerospace; Ahuti Mk II: 498 km/h.

topics.title: Environment and Ecology: Clean Air, Aravalli, Lichens, Land Restoration and SAF
facts: The 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards were presented on Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 to assess city and ward performance in air-pollution management under the National Clean Air Programme.

The Supreme Court directed the High-Powered Committee on Aravalli Hills/Ranges demarcation to submit a final, non-extendable report by 30 November 2026; the region covers Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi and Gujarat.
Buellia maharajensis, a new lichen species, was discovered at about 1,351 m in Mathikettan Shola National Park, Kerala, highlighting Western Ghats cryptic biodiversity.
UNCCD COP17 discussions focused on drought resilience, land restoration, financing and protection of pastoral communities, with India emphasising land restoration and open natural ecosystems.
Akasa Air operated a Mumbai–Goa commercial flight using BPCL-supplied ATF blended with 1% sustainable aviation fuel; India’s target is 5% SAF blending by 2030.
topics.detail: Environmental affairs covered clean-air performance, judicial protection of the Aravallis, Western Ghats biodiversity, land restoration and sustainable aviation.
topics.exam: NCAP, Aravalli geography, lichen biodiversity, UNCCD and SAF blending are relevant for UPSC environment and geography questions.
topics.remember: Aravalli deadline: 30 November 2026; new lichen: Buellia maharajensis; Akasa Air SAF blend: 1%; 2030 target: 5%.

topics.title: Defence and Security: DAC Approvals, Exercises, AASHVAST, SHIELD and AK-203
facts: The Defence Acquisition Council approved capital-acquisition proposals worth about ₹1.10 lakh crore at the Acceptance of Necessity stage, covering Army vehicles, helicopters, mine-laying systems, bridge systems, Navy radars and marine gas turbines, and IAF electronic and aircraft capabilities.

India–USA joint exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 began on 9 September at Bikaner, Rajasthan and Auli, Uttarakhand; the 22nd edition focuses on interoperability, readiness, information sharing and emerging battlefield technologies.
Indian and Japanese Air Forces began Veer Guardian-2026 at Jodhpur from 9–22 September, involving Indian LCA Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale aircraft and Japanese F-2A fighters.

The Indian Army established AASHVAST—Assessment and Analysis of Electronic Systems Hardware for Vulnerabilities and Security Threats—at DG EME headquarters, New Delhi, to identify foreign components and vulnerabilities in unmanned systems and drones.

DRDO launched SHIELD—S-band High-Power Microwave Integrated Evaluation for Lethality and Damage—to test electronic-system vulnerability using high-power microwave and Gallium Nitride-based SSPA technology, with DTTF-supported industry participation.
Adani Defence & Aerospace and Indo-Russian Rifles signed an agreement for 7.62×39 mm AK-203 ammunition manufactured at Kanpur; AK-203 rifles are produced at Korwa, Amethi.
topics.detail: Defence updates combined major capital-acquisition approvals, India’s bilateral exercises with the USA and Japan, electronic-vulnerability assessment and indigenous small-arms ammunition production.
topics.exam: Know the full forms of AASHVAST and SHIELD, the locations of Yudh Abhyas and Veer Guardian, and the ₹1.10 lakh crore DAC approval value.

hi.title: रक्षा एवं सुरक्षा: DAC approvals, Exercises, AASHVAST, SHIELD और AK-203
facts: Defence Acquisition Council ने Acceptance of Necessity stage पर लगभग ₹1.10 लाख करोड़ के capital-acquisition proposals को मंजूरी दी; Army vehicles, helicopters, mine-laying systems, bridges, Navy radars/marine gas turbines तथा IAF electronic और aircraft capabilities शामिल हैं।

India–USA joint exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 9 सितंबर को Bikaner और Auli में शुरू हुआ; 22nd edition का focus interoperability, operational readiness, information sharing और emerging battlefield technologies पर है।
Indian और Japanese Air Forces ने 9–22 सितंबर तक Jodhpur में Veer Guardian-2026 शुरू किया; Indian LCA Tejas, Su-30MKI और Rafale तथा Japanese F-2A fighters शामिल हैं।

Indian Army ने DG EME headquarters, New Delhi में AASHVAST lab स्थापित की। इसका full form Assessment and Analysis of Electronic Systems Hardware for Vulnerabilities and Security Threats है और उद्देश्य unmanned systems/drones में foreign components तथा vulnerabilities पहचानना है।

DRDO ने SHIELD programme launch किया। इसका full form S-band High-Power Microwave Integrated Evaluation for Lethality and Damage है; high-power microwave, Gallium Nitride-based SSPA और electronic-system vulnerability testing पर focus है।
Adani Defence & Aerospace और Indo-Russian Rifles ने 7.62×39 mm AK-203 ammunition supply agreement किया; ammunition Kanpur में और AK-203 rifles Korwa, Amethi में बनती हैं।
hi.detail: Defence updates में capital-acquisition approvals, USA और Japan के साथ bilateral exercises, electronic-vulnerability assessment तथा indigenous small-arms ammunition production शामिल रहे।

topics.title: Sports: China Masters, Women’s Asia Cup, Para Archery and Asian Games
facts: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty won the China Masters men’s doubles title by defeating He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu; it was India’s first men’s doubles title at the China Masters.
India defeated Pakistan by seven wickets in the Women’s Asia Cup; Shree Charani and Prema Rawat took three wickets each, while Shafali Verma reached 3,000 T20I career runs during the period.
India won five medals at Stage 3 of the World Archery Para Series in Ahmedabad: two gold, two silver and one bronze.
India’s Asian Games 2026 contingent received a grand send-off in New Delhi from the Sports Ministry and Indian Olympic Association.
The US Open men’s singles final was held on 13 September, outside the 6–12 September window; the later Alexander Zverev result is therefore excluded from this week’s compilation.
topics.detail: Sports coverage included badminton, women’s cricket, para archery, India’s Asian Games preparation and a clear date-boundary note for the US Open.

topics.title: Appointments and Changes: Adobe, Andaman and Nicobar, High Courts and APPU
facts: Anil Chakravarthy was appointed Adobe’s next President and CEO, effective 1 December 2026; Shantanu Narayen will transition to Executive Chair.
Former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and Rajya Sabha MP Dr Dinesh Sharma was appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, succeeding Admiral D.K. Joshi.

Eight High Court judges were appointed Chief Justices, including V. Kameswar Rao at Patna, Ravindra V. Ghuge at Calcutta, Sanjay Kumar Agrawal at Rajasthan, Mahesh Chandra Tripathi at Bombay, Ashwani Kumar Mishra at Punjab & Haryana, Krushna Ram Mohapatra at Chhattisgarh, Alpesh Yeshwant Kogje at Madhya Pradesh and Pushpendra Singh Bhati at J&K and Ladakh.
Dr Vinaya Prakash Singh was re-elected for a second term as Secretary-General of the Asian-Pacific Postal Union for 2027–2030.

topics.title: UNESCO Tentative List Additions and Dogri Script
facts: Four Indian heritage sites were added to the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List: Rangpur-Sivasagar Historic Ensemble in Assam, Colonial Penal Settlement in the Andaman Islands, Nicobarese Cultural Continuity in Nicobar and Painted Havelis of Shekhawati in Rajasthan.
The additions took India’s UNESCO Tentative List total to 73 sites.
Preservation and revival efforts concerning the Dogri language and Dogri script in the Jammu region remained in focus; Dogri is among India’s recognised regional languages.

facts: Uttar Pradesh: Meerut ITI cluster received ₹240.40 crore PM-SETU investment; WDFC connectivity reached Dadri; Kanpur’s AK-203 ammunition ecosystem and 24 UP organisations in ChipIN were highlighted.
Gujarat: PM Modi visited Vadodara; WDFC sections and railway/highway projects were highlighted along with renewable and industrial connectivity.
Maharashtra: Mumbai hosted Global Fintech Fest and JNPT remained central to WDFC connectivity.
Rajasthan: Bhiwadi received ₹241 crore PM-SETU investment; Bikaner hosted Yudh Abhyas and Jodhpur hosted Veer Guardian.
Telangana: Medchal received ₹254.30 crore PM-SETU investment and Telangana was a major ChipIN contributor.
Chhattisgarh ranked first nationally in Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB 3.0) and presented a water-conservation model under Catch the Rain.
Madhya Pradesh: ADB renewable-energy PPP transaction advisory agreement with potential private investment of US$1 billion.
Kerala: Mathikettan Shola National Park yielded the new lichen Buellia maharajensis.

Odisha: 14 MoUs with UAE-based International Holding Company and Adani Group indicated nearly ₹2.1 lakh crore in projects across AI data centres, coal-to-chemicals, minerals, renewable energy, shipbuilding, petrochemicals, ports and healthcare.
Punjab: Pehchaan Portal was launched for unidentified and unclaimed deceased persons; the portal integrates MedLeaPR and CCTNS.
Jharkhand: Amended BharatNet agreement worth about ₹1,684 crore targets 4,395 Gram Panchayats.
